newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq's Aziz slams U.N. sanctions, hits out at U.S..
newsitem.headline: Iraq's Aziz slams U.N. sanctions, hits out at U.S..

text.p: Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz said on Sunday the U.N. embargo imposed on Iraq for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait was tantamount to a genocide against the Iraqi people.

"They (U.S. and allies) persist with the imposition of embargo on the Iraqi people, denying the Iraqis not the export of oil but the morsel, bottle of medicine, the machine, paper, pens and feather," said Aziz in an address to Arab poets and writers.

Aziz said those behind the embargo wanted to destroy Iraq "as a people and homeland...annihilate Iraq so that it will never rise again" and he lambasted the United States as the "most insolent of colonial tyrants the world has ever known."
Iraq is barred under the U.N. sanctions from exporting oil. The sanctions also prohibit trade with Baghdad excluding humanitarian items.
The literary gathering in Baghdad was the second since the 1991 Gulf War over Kuwait in which a U.S.-led multi-national force drove Iraqi troops out of the Gulf state.
In the 1980s hundreds of Arab poets and writers used to take part in the gathering but this year renowned poets from Egypt, Syria and other Arab countries stayed away.
Some 20 Iraqi poets in exile, among them Abdulwahab al- Bayati, Iraq's best-know poet abroad, have denounced the festival as "a propaganda stint."
Bahrain, United Arab Emirates, Oman, Qatar, Lebanon, Jordan, Tunis and Sudan were among the countries represented.
